verdict.rationale: Stripe documents restricted API keys (RAKs) with per-resource Read/Write/None permissions and explicitly recommends them when giving a key to an AI agent. It also supports agent-scoped use: OAuth sessions for MCP with per-session revoke, separate live and sandbox controls, and restricted keys limited to specific connected-account permissions. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that agent-scoped RAKs work as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Stripe recommends always using RAKs instead of unrestricted secret keys, especially when giving a key to an AI agent. Use RAK permissions to limit what an agent can do in your account.
a RAK can do only what you give it permission to do.
authenticate with a restricted API key for your platform and grant only the connected-account permissions that your agent needs.
OAuth lets you grant and revoke access without sharing an API key with the client
